reason: E1 shows that configurational and thermal entropy contributions can be separated and that configurational entropy differences between fcc materials (pure Ni vs. Cantor alloy) affect total entropy, supporting the first two premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that varying Cu content in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles alters configurational entropy or that such changes govern premelting/melting behavior; E2 only describes powder mixing and does not address thermodynamics or phase transitions.
premises: Configurational entropy and thermal entropy contributions can be separated and their sum determines Gibbs free energy
For fcc alloys, configurational entropy differences (e.g., pure Ni vs. Cantor alloy) lead to distinct total entropy inputs
Copper content in FeNiCrCoCu HEA nanoparticles alters configurational entropy
Changes in configurational entropy from Cu content will measurably shift premelting and melting behavior
